implementation_notes: Kotlin's stdlib read-only types are views, not immutability - the collections overview stresses that 'a mutable collection doesn't have to be assigned to a var' - so the snapshot guarantee comes from the kotlinx.collections.immutable library: ImmutableList/ImmutableMap are immutable, PersistentList/PersistentMap additionally share structure so plus/minus 'may share storage with the original collection', and persistentListOf/persistentMapOf (or toPersistentList()) build them. Publication is java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference with compareAndSet/updateAndGet on the JVM, or kotlinx.atomicfu for multiplatform, and @Volatile for a plain field written by one owner; on the JVM java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList remains the right tool for read-mostly listener lists. The counted body itself is never hand-written - the GC owns the reference count.
pitfalls: Read-only is not immutable: a MutableList<Int> is a List<Int>, so a property typed List can be mutated through another reference - only the kotlinx immutable/persistent types (or a defensive copy) give the snapshot guarantee the pattern needs.

Atomics are not portable: java.util.concurrent.atomic is JVM-only, so Kotlin/Native and Kotlin/JS need kotlinx.atomicfu (or a coroutine Mutex), and mixing per-platform publication is where contention bugs creep in.

Coroutines add a suspension trap the atomics do not cover: a writer that clones the snapshot and then suspends before publishing can publish a stale value over a newer one - clone and publish without suspension points, or serialise writers with a Mutex plus a version check.
sources: Kotlin documentation, Collections overview - read-only versus mutable interfaces, and 'a mutable collection doesn't have to be assigned to a var': https://kotlinlang.org/docs/collections-overview.html

kotlinx.collections.immutable (JetBrains) README - immutable and persistent collection interfaces, and plus/minus returning a collection that 'may share storage with the original collection': https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.collections.immutable
